messages:
sri: Heads-up — noticed a ~22% drop in token-saved from the prefix cache for redwood-13b in us-west over the last 6h. Spike shows up ~02:15 UTC. Anyone picking this up?
perf-bot: Alert: prefix_cache_token_saved_drop for redwood-13b/us-west triggered at 2026-03-18T02:20:10Z (severity=warning) — lookback=6h
aj: I see it on the token-saved rollup. Key-based hit-rate is ~1-2% down but token-weighted hit-rate is worse — suggests misses on long prompts (high token penalty).
danielle: FWIW I deployed whitespace normalization (trim + collapse multi-spaces) in PR #423. Canary -> 01:40, prod -> 02:05. That could change keys for any cache that used raw prompt strings.
sri: timeline matches. If normalization changed the exact key shape, old cached prefixes won't match -> misses on heavy customers.
leo: we should measure key stability. Two quick signals: overlap_rate (old_key -> new_key mapping %) and token_loss_by_tenant (tokens saved before vs after).
aj: running a quick extraction against the observability store. Query proto:
```
-- approximate SQL for overlap rate
WITH recent AS (SELECT tenant_id, prefix_hash_old, prefix_hash_new, tokens FROM prefix_cache_log WHERE model='redwood-13b' AND region='us-west' AND ts BETWEEN now()-interval '8 hours' AND now())
SELECT tenant_id,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN prefix_hash_old = prefix_hash_new THEN 1 END) / COUNT(*) AS overlap_pct,
  SUM(CASE WHEN prefix_hash_old != prefix_hash_new THEN tokens END) AS token_loss_tokens
FROM recent
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY token_loss_tokens DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
aj: results coming — top 3 tenants show overlap_pct ~65-72% and token_loss_tokens concentrated on two enterprise customers.
danielle: ugh, my change collapses multiple spaces which would change many prompt prefixes that include pasted examples. I can roll a hotfix to preserve intra-line spacing for prefixes under 1k chars to reduce churn. Thoughts?
sri: good idea. Before quick fix, can we do a short-lived fallback in runtime: try normalized key first, if miss then try legacy key lookup (fast double-hash probe) for 30m? That preserves hit-rate while we roll correction. Need to confirm perf impact of double-probe.
leo: double-probe is cheap if we short-circuit on hit and only probes for misses. I'll bench it on canary; expected tail latency increase ~0.3-0.6ms p95 per request (mostly metadata lookups).
ops-bot: Note: would add ~0.5 RPS per node for key-lookup traffic estimate. Ops flagged for capacity if we enable region-wide.
aj: bench on canary (small pool) — double-probe p50 unaffected, p95 +0.4ms, no OOMs. Token-saved recovers ~80% for canary traffic.
danielle: OK I'll open a rollback+patch: (a) enable double-probe runtime fallback for 30m, (b) revert whitespace normalization in prod for prefix key path, (c) release improved normalization that keeps prefix hashing stable. PRs: #436 runtime fallback, #437 revert key path, #438 stable-normalize.
sri: action items: @leo enable #436 on canary now, @aj monitor token-saved + token-weighted hit-rate dashboard, @danielle prepare #437 and #438, ops keep an eye on node load. We'll reconvene in 25m. :thumbsup:
aj: I'm attaching the quick dashboard query I used to track token-weighted hit-rate by tenant: `sum(tokens_saved_when_hit)/sum(tokens_total)` grouped by tenant and model; export top-50 tenants. Helps prioritize who to protect first.
leo: rolling fallback to canary (pool: runtime-canary-3) now. Patch ID: fb9c2.
sri: thanks — if we see recovery in canary, we push fallback region-wide and then do the normalization patch properly. Also add an observability panel: 'legacy-key-probe-rate' to detect how often fallback fires post-fix.
perf-bot: Note: Incident created: INC-20260318-1147 prefix-cache-drop — assignees: leo, aj, danielle — severity=high if token-saved not >90% baseline in 2h.
sri: keeping thread here. If anyone notices similar on other models (redwood-7b, open-llama), ping and we'll run same overlap check. Thanks everyone.
